title: Canonical coefficient comparisons of the supported-Kummer affine orientation
statement: In the fixed setting [def-pur-conventions], let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $s:Y\to\mathbf A^1_Y$ its zero section. The ordinary supported Kummer boundary [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary] and [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-system] uniquely determines its supported Ext class at exponent $\ell^n$, for every $n\ge1$. Its exceptional adjunct, transported to the intrinsic small pro-etale category, defines the canonical affine orientation $A_Y\to Rs^! A_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. For the actual finite reduction [def-pur-finite-reduction-root-charts], the coefficient-unit and counit comparisons [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons] define: (i) the isomorphism reducing its shifted Tate-line input, uniquely normalized in all compatible primitive-root charts; (ii) the zero-section exceptional coefficient map, uniquely characterized by the compact-support transpose of the reduced exceptional counit. These comparisons use no orientation to specify their maps and impose no divisibility of the level by the ramification index.
